name: gemm
notes:
One program for every (m, k, n): the shape reaches it through CRs and four loops -- the
token loop (dynamic, m rows of y), the output-channel tile loop (one row of R_ACC is 128 channels),
the k chunk loop (a's 128-lane rows) and the input loop inside a chunk -- so a whole layer
(4096 tokens x 1024 channels x 2880 inputs) is one launch, not one launch per tile, and the host
only launches. a is token-major (token i's k elements in rows i*chunks+c); w is *input-major*, row
t*wtiles+tt holding input channel t's weights for the tile of channels tt*128..tt*128+127 (column n
pads the last tile, row k the input loop's last prefetch); b is the n biases in its own region, one
row per tile; y is one row per token and tile. The inner loop is the outer product: one word does
MULT.RC.VE of the tile's 128 weights (R_CYCLIC slot 0) against the scalar a[i,t] (R0[t mod 128]) and
ACC.ADD into the tile's 128 FP32 accumulators, so each word is 128 useful MACs and the whole of k is
contracted inside the kernel -- no partial ever leaves XMEM and no host step joins anything. The word
also prefetches the next input's w row (MULT reads R_CYCLIC at cycle start) and advances the two
counters kept one ahead, so the multiply, the accumulate, the load and the branch all ride in one
word; the tile's b row sits in R1 for the whole pass, which lets the store word do the bias add
(MULT.VE x CR1 + ACC.ADD) and ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE identity in the same word. A short last chunk stops
at k - 128*(chunks-1) inputs and lanes past k multiply the packer's zeros, so nothing is wasted on
the k tail; the store's DS names 128 lanes for a full tile and n - 128*(ytiles-1) for the last, so a
row's scale never sees a lane past n. Every instruction is a hardware one, the golden is a float64
matmul of the values XMEM holds, and the cases pass with the store's quantization as the only
rounding (max |err| inside one step of the row grid). Domain: m 1..4096, k 1..2944, n 1..1024,
act only "none" (an activation is another ke

name: row_norm_layernorm
notes:
One parameterised program for every (kind, rows, channels): layernorm
y[r] = (x[r] - mean_r) * A_r * gamma + beta and rmsnorm y[r] = x[r] * A_r * gamma, with
A_r = rsqrt(max(var_r, eps)) taken by the AaQ stage's hardware rsqrt (the approximation; the
variance is floored at eps by ACC.MAX first so the rsqrt never sees a negative). The shape
reaches the program through CRs and the row loop is dynamic, so a whole layer -- 1024 tokens x
144 channels -- is one launch; the host only launches (it may tile `rows`, the one dimension the
kernel does not loop over on its own, while `channels` is the kernel's own chunk loop, rendered
per call). x and y are the chip's activation layout (entity r owns ceil(channels/128) consecutive
rows, lanes past channels zero), so the output is the next kernel's input unchanged; gamma, beta,
the 1/channels and eps constant rows and the mask row are constants prepared offline. Dataflow,
per group of up to 128 rows whose bookkeeping lives one value per R_ACC lane: two reduction
passes at one word per (row, chunk) each (MULT.RC.VV of the row against the resident 1/channels
row then AGG.SUM, so the mean reduces directly with no quantized sum in front of it; then
MULT.RC.VS and AGG.SUM for the squares), the group's scalars straight-line (A = rsqrt of
squares/channels - mean^2 floored at eps, D = -(mean*A)), then p = A_r*x + D_r and y = p*gamma +
beta at two words per (row, chunk) -- a word holds one multiply-accumulate pair and y's three
products cannot meet in one of them, so the intermediate is stored once; rmsnorm needs neither D
nor beta and runs three words per (row, chunk). Every operand address is a CR base plus an LR
row, every LR is set before it is read, R_ACC is zeroed before each reduction and R_MASK is
loaded from its own row, so the program runs after another kernel as well as from reset (the
folder's test_calls.py runs the kernel twice back to back on one XMEM, the second reading the
